questions.question: Who should see an agent's internal reasoning?
options: Developers, through a trace; the user sees the answer
questions.explanation: Reasoning is valuable for debugging, and noise or even a leak risk in a user-facing reply.

questions.question: What does the think tool return, and why?
options: The answer, computed from the thought
Just 'ok': its value is giving the model a place to reason between actions, not new information
An error, to force a retry
questions.explanation: It's a no-op tool. The thought itself lands in the history and the trace.

questions.question: Old messages are trimmed to save tokens. How does a looked-up fact survive?
options: The agent saved it with note(), and notes are pinned into the system prompt on every turn
questions.explanation: Pinned notes are re-rendered each turn, independent of which messages are kept.

questions.question: Why must trimmed history never start with a tool message?
options: A tool result without its assistant tool call is an orphan; most APIs reject it
questions.explanation: Every tool result must follow the assistant message that requested it.

questions.question: In 20 live runs, llama3.2 never called the think tool, and every run took exactly 2 steps. What's the likely cause?
options: Its chat template shows tools only with the last user message, so after one tool call the model sees no tools at all
Think tools only work with OpenAI
questions.explanation: With one tool-visible turn per run, spending it on 'think' would mean never calling a real tool.

questions.question: Re-prompting after tool results kept tools visible: runs got longer and lookups succeeded, but correctness didn't improve. What's the takeaway?
options: Fixing tool visibility removed one blocker; the small model's reasoning is the next one. Measure each fix separately
questions.explanation: One fix, one measured effect. Don't expect a plumbing fix to make a 3B model reason well.
